query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: An optimized rapid thermal annealing (RTA) treatment of a near‐equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with an fcc structure will enhance its coercivity compared to the as-cast baseline by inducing a refined nanocrystalline microstructure that increases magnetic domain wall pinning.
generation.material_initial_state: An as‐cast, near‐equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy exhibiting a predominantly fcc structure, high saturation magnetization, and soft ferromagnetic behavior with low coercivity.
generation.intervention: Apply a tailored rapid thermal annealing (RTA) process with reduced temperature and short duration under inert atmosphere.
generation.conditions: The annealing must be performed at a temperature high enough to activate limited atomic mobility for grain refinement but well below the level that would induce phase segregation or decomposition, and under an inert atmosphere to preserve alloy purity and high configurational entropy.
generation.structural_mediator: A refined nanocrystalline microstructure featuring a higher density of grain boundaries (or localized nanoscale chemical order) that can serve as effective pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
generation.mechanism: The RTA-induced grain refinement increases the number of domain wall pinning sites, thereby raising the energy barrier for domain wall motion. This improved pinning enhances the coercive field while largely maintaining the high saturation magnetization of the alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: The treated alloy is expected to exhibit a measurable increase in coercivity relative to the untreated as-cast state, without compromising its high saturation magnetization and equiatomic high-entropy characteristics.
generation.baseline: The as-cast near‐equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with larger grain sizes and soft magnetic properties (low coercivity).
generation.boundary: If the RTA parameters (temperature or time) exceed the optimal window, the alloy may experience unwanted phase decomposition or grain coarsening, which would compromise both its high-entropy stability and magnetic performance.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of coercivity enhancement and its reproducibility require further experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of near‐equiatomic FeCoNi-based alloy samples: one set as-cast (control) and the other set subjected to the optimized RTA treatment. Use X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to verify that the alloy remains a single-phase fcc structure and to quantify grain size refinement. Perform magnetic hysteresis measurements (using vibrating sample magnetometry) on both sets to compare coercivity and saturation magnetization.
measurements: TEM for grain size and microstructural refinement
VSM hysteresis loops for coercivity (Hc) and saturation magnetization (Ms)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the RTA-treated samples do not show a statistically significant increase (e.g., at least a 20% enhancement) in coercivity compared to the as-cast baseline, or if the microstructural analysis reveals phase decomposition or loss of high-entropy single-phase character, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Therefore, the bimodal coercivity distribution observed in the OOP direction is explained by a 2‐step process of magnetization reversal beginning with easy domain nucleation and propagation in the large (001) oriented grains (narrow low Hc peak), followed by pinning between grains with small size and varying easy‐axis direction (broad high Hc peak). The distribution of size and easy‐axis orientation both manifest in the spreading of the high Hc peak along the Hc axis. Based on this, we expect that the Hc could be enhanced through microstructural optimization such as a reduction in grain size, which may be achieved by adjusting the RTA time and temperature.

A high entropy single-phase product with a perovskite structure was obtained in the present work. The calculated formula of the substituted phase was Na0.30K0.07Ca0.24La0.18Ce0.21TiO3. From the PXRD data, it was concluded that the high entropy sample was the single perovskite phase. The electrodynamic investigation was performed the morphology, chemical composition, crystal structure, and dielectric properties were studied and compared with pure barium titanate BaTiO3 matrix. The polysubstituted high entropy single-phase product contains five doping elements at a high concentration level. The dielectric measurements were performed. The significant influence of high entropy composition on the microcrystals properties was observed. Due to these results, this material can be used in the electric device’s design.

drafts.hypothesis: Replacing the noble metal (Pd or Pt) in FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys with tungsten will promote increased lattice distortion and induce local phase heterogeneity, resulting in enhanced domain‐wall pinning that increases the alloy’s coercivity.
drafts.material_initial_state: FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys such as FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt that form predominantly fcc structures and exhibit soft ferromagnetism.
drafts.intervention: Substitute the Pd or Pt component with tungsten to produce an equiatomic FeCoNiW high-entropy alloy.
drafts.conditions: The alloy must remain near-equiatomic with a configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Processing should allow sufficient atomic diffusion for tungsten to induce lattice strain and possibly nucleate localized secondary (e.g., minor bcc) phases within an overall fcc matrix.
drafts.structural_mediator: Enhanced lattice distortion and the potential formation of localized, harder magnetic regions due to phase heterogeneity introduced by tungsten’s larger atomic size.
drafts.mechanism: W tungsten’s larger atomic radius compared to Pd or Pt increases lattice strain when incorporated into the FeCoNi matrix. This strain can promote the nucleation of minor, magnetically harder phases or regions within the predominantly fcc structure. These regions act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls, thus raising the coercivity relative to the soft ferromagnetic baseline.
drafts.predicted_outcome: The FeCoNiW alloy will exhibit a higher coercive field than the FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys while retaining a high saturation magnetization, provided that the structural changes (lattice distortions/secondary phase formation) are effectively induced.
drafts.baseline: FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt high-entropy alloys that are soft ferromagnetic with low coercivity.
drafts.boundary: The effect is expected only if the alloy remains near-equiatomic and is processed under conditions that allow sufficient atomic mobility for tungsten-induced lattice distortion and phase heterogeneity. Deviations in composition or processing may suppress the effect.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize an equiatomic FeCoNiW high-entropy alloy alongside FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt controls under identical processing conditions. Characterize the crystal structure and microstructure using X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy, then measure the magnetic hysteresis loops to extract coercivity and saturation magnetization.
measurements: X-ray diffraction for phase identification and lattice parameter determination
Electron microscopy for microstructural analysis and detection of secondary phases
Magnetic hysteresis loop measurements to quantify coercivity and saturation magnetization
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the FeCoNiW alloy does not show a statistically greater coercive field compared to the FeCoNiPd/FeCoNiPt alloys, or if no significant lattice distortions or minor phase regions are detected, then the hypothesis is falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: A post‐processing heat treatment that induces nanoscale chemical short‐range order can increase the coercivity of an equiatomic FeCoNiPd high‐entropy alloy relative to its as‐cast soft magnetic state.
drafts.material_initial_state: An as‐cast, almost equiatomic FeCoNiPd high‐entropy alloy with an fcc structure, high saturation magnetization, and low coercivity.
drafts.intervention: Apply a two‐step annealing process (i.e. intermediate temperature anneal followed by quenching) designed to mobilize atomic rearrangements without triggering full phase segregation.
drafts.conditions: The heat treatment must be performed at a temperature range high enough for limited atomic diffusion but below that for complete phase separation, in an inert atmosphere to prevent oxidation.
drafts.structural_mediator: Nanoscale regions of chemical short‐range order within the overall fcc matrix.
drafts.mechanism: The locally ordered regions provide heterogeneities that serve as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls. Their presence increases the energy barrier for domain wall motion, thereby raising the coercive field while retaining high saturation magnetization.
drafts.predicted_outcome: The annealed alloy will show a measurable increase in coercivity (domain‐wall pinning effect) compared to the as‐cast (baseline) state, while still maintaining the desired high-entropy (≥1.0R configurational entropy) equiatomic composition and fcc structure.
drafts.baseline: The untreated (as‐cast) equiatomic FeCoNiPd alloy known to exhibit relatively soft ferromagnetism.
drafts.boundary: If the annealing parameters (temperature or time) exceed the optimal window, the alloy may undergo excessive phase segregation or structural transformation, which could compromise both its high magnetization and the targeted coercivity increase.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of equiatomic FeCoNiPd samples: one set is left as-cast (baseline) and the other is subjected to the proposed two-step annealing treatment. Characterize both sets using X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy to assess the presence of nanoscale chemical short-range order, and use vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM) to obtain hysteresis loops.
measurements: XRD for detection of any ordering-related peak broadening or superlattice reflections
TEM to directly image the nanoscale regions with chemical short-range order
Magnetic hysteresis measurements (coercivity, remanence, saturation magnetization)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed samples do not exhibit a significant increase (e.g., at least ~20%) in coercivity compared to the as-cast samples, or if they show evidence of undesirable phase segregation (loss of the fcc structure), the hypothesis is falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: A rapid thermal annealing (RTA) treatment that refines the microstructure of a near‐equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy will increase its coercivity by enhancing domain wall pinning without reducing its high saturation magnetization.
drafts.material_initial_state: A chemically disordered, single-phase, near‐equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy (with at least five principal elements to ensure a configurational entropy above 1.0R) produced by conventional melt processing that exhibits an fcc structure with relatively large grains and soft ferromagnetism.
drafts.intervention: Subject the alloy to a tailored RTA process (i.e. a short-duration, lower-temperature anneal) designed to arrest grain growth and induce significant grain size refinement.
drafts.conditions: Perform the RTA under an inert atmosphere at a temperature below the conventional recrystallization point (for example, near 600°C) for a short time (on the order of minutes) so that the alloy remains single phase and high in entropy while developing a nanocrystalline microstructure.
drafts.structural_mediator: Nanocrystalline grain structure with a higher density of grain boundaries.
drafts.mechanism: The refined nanostructure increases the number of effective pinning sites for magnetic domain walls, thereby enhancing magnetocrystalline anisotropy and increasing the coercive field. The shorter annealing time prevents unwanted grain growth that would otherwise lead to a soft magnetic response.
drafts.predicted_outcome: The RTA-treated FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy is expected to show a measurable increase in coercivity (e.g., by more than 20% compared to conventionally processed samples) while largely retaining high saturation magnetization.
drafts.baseline: FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys (including earlier derivatives with Pd or Pt) processed without such microstructural refinement, which present an fcc structure with larger grains and low coercivity (i.e., soft ferromagnetism).
drafts.boundary: This effect is expected only if the processing maintains the single-phase character and high configurational entropy of the alloy. Over-annealing or using temperatures high enough to promote significant grain growth or phase decomposition would negate the coercivity enhancement.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a batch of the near‐equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy and split it into two groups. Subject one group to the tailored RTA treatment (e.g., anneal at ~600°C for 15 minutes under inert atmosphere) and keep the other group as a control processed by standard cooling. Characterize both groups using transmission electron microscopy (to measure grain size) and vibrating sample magnetometry (to obtain magnetic hysteresis curves).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the RTA-treated samples do not show a statistically significant increase (e.g., >20% relative to control) in coercivity while retaining high saturation magnetization, or if the unique nanocrystalline microstructure is not confirmed, then the hypothesis is falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: Optimizing the rapid thermal annealing (RTA) process to induce grain refinement in an equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy will enhance coercivity by increasing domain wall pinning compared to conventional processing or previously reported FeCoNiPt alloys.
drafts.material_initial_state: An almost equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with a predominantly fcc structure and high configurational entropy (≥1.0R)
drafts.intervention: Apply an optimized RTA treatment with a lower annealing temperature and a controlled shorter annealing time to achieve significant grain size reduction without decomposition into undesired secondary phases
drafts.conditions: This intervention should be performed on FeCoNi-based HEAs prepared under similar synthesis conditions, ensuring the alloy remains a stable single-phase high-entropy solid solution; the RTA parameters must be tuned to produce a nanostructured microstructure
drafts.structural_mediator: Grain size reduction and an increased density of grain boundaries, which serve as effective pinning centers for magnetic domain walls
drafts.mechanism: The refined grain structure enhances domain wall pinning, thereby impeding the motion of magnetic domains during reversal. This increased energy barrier for domain wall movement results in higher coercivity while preserving high saturation magnetization
drafts.predicted_outcome: The optimized RTA-treated alloy will exhibit a significantly higher coercivity—beyond that of conventional FeCoNi processing and previously studied FeCoNiPt derivatives—while maintaining its high saturation magnetization
drafts.baseline: FeCoNi-based HEA processed under conventional RTA conditions that result in relatively larger grain sizes and soft ferromagnetic behavior
drafts.boundary: The intervention is effective provided that the annealing conditions yield grain sizes small enough to boost coercivity but do not induce unwanted phase decomposition. The alloy must remain within the single-phase high-entropy regime

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of FeCoNi-based HEA samples: one set processed under conventional RTA conditions and another set processed under optimized low-temperature, short-duration RTA designed for grain refinement. Characterize their microstructures via SEM/TEM and measure their magnetic hysteresis loops using a vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized RTA-treated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in coercivity (e.g., a >20% improvement) relative to the baseline samples, or if the process inadvertently induces phase decomposition that compromises the HEA’s single-phase integrity, the hypothesis must be rejected.
